name: The drying shed at Miller and Hall's tanyard

documented_range.note: NO SOURCE RECORD DATES THIS BUILDING, BECAUSE NO SOURCE RECORD NAMES IT. The bracket is the tanyard's own, carried across without being re-argued: `miller_tannery` - the log house Samuel Miller's brother John used as a tannery, with Benjamin Hall in from 1832 - carries 1831-01-01 to 1835-12-31, and a yard building that serves that tannery cannot honestly claim to have stood before it. Graded `reconstructed`, as the building is.

position.symbolic_location: On the point of land at the forks, in the yard behind John Miller's tannery, at the inner end of the back row with its west wall on the tannery's own east wall line and its door facing south across the yard.
position.note:
INVENTED, AND SEATED BY THE WORKS RULE BELOW. THE TANYARD RUNS NORTH, BEHIND THE TANNERY, AND THAT IS WHERE THE GROUND IS. `miller_tannery` stands at bearing 180 with its face south toward Samuel Miller's house and tavern; behind it is north, on the point of land between the North Branch and the main stem. The two yard buildings stand side by side across that back yard, both with their front walls on one line 5.20 m north of the tannery's north wall - the cart yard figure T-1640 derived from `data/yard/town_trade_goods.json` - and each with one wall on one of the tannery's own two side walls, so the yard is framed by the three buildings rather than scattered behind one. THIS BUILDING takes the INNER seat of the back row: its west wall stands on local E 14.000, which is the tannery's own east wall line, and its front wall stands at local N 83.200 - the same line as the bark shed's, which stands 2.00 m further east, so the two read as one row and not as two sheds. MEASURED ON THIS SEAT, over a 25 x 25 lattice on the placed polygon: the ground stands 1.138 m to 1.140 m above the committed water surface - dry, with 0.002 m of relief; `intrusion` reads it clear of all 33 platted corridors; and the nearest committed footprint is the tannery's own north wall at 5.20 m. WORKING UNCERTAINTY: the site is the tannery's, which is `inferred`; the building is entirely invented.

THE WORKS RULE, STATED ONCE AND APPLIED SIX TIMES (T-1709). Every one of the four documented noxious trades on the branches records, in its own footprint note, that the works are outside its polygon: `newberry_dole_slaughterhouse_south_branch` says 'the pens, the yard and the barrelling and salting space that a packing operation needs are outside the footprint and outside this archetype, which builds a building rather than a works'; `miller_tannery` says 'a tannery is its yard - bark mill, lime pits, tan vats, drying sheds, and a water supply - and none of that is in this polygon or in the model'; `clybourn_slaughterhouse` says 'what is not modelled is arguably the bigger half'; `elston_soap_candle_manufactory` gives a shed 'big enough for a rendering kettle, a cooling and moulding floor and an ash leach' and nothing beside it. This building is one of the works those four sentences name, and NOTHING ATTESTS IT. It is placed by a rule and not by a plate. THE RULE: (1) a works building stands BEHIND its plant, on the side away from the water, because the plant's own bearing puts its working face on the water and the ground behind it is what is left; (2) the gap between the plant's wall and the works' wall is 5.20 m, the cart yard T-1640 derived from `data/yard/town_trade_goods.json` - 1.00 m of clearance from the wall a wagon stands at, plus the 3.20 m of ground a parked wagon needs, plus 1.00 m from the wall opposite - and the same 5.20 m separates one works building from the next, so the whole band is set out on one committed figure; (3) the works take the plant's own bearing, so the yard between them is square and the doors face it; (4) where the ground behind the plant is a platted street corridor, the works stand ALONG the bank instead, in the order the work runs, on a line that keeps them 0.50 m clear of that corridor's own edge - which is what the South Branch band does, because Market Street's corridor runs E 73.00 to E 97.00 at this reach and the plant itself stands 1.30 m inside it. THE FOUR PREDICATES each seat is held to, on a 25 x 25 lattice over the placed polygon: dry in the committed heightfield (`data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut`, WATER_SURFACE_M = 0), relief inside the 0.30 m `generate_block_infill.MAX_RELIEF_M` allows, clear of all 33 platted corridors (`tools/plat_corridors.intrusion`), and clear of every footprint the committed tree already places. docs/RESEARCH/branch_noxious_works.md carries the readings and docs/LIBERTIES.md L284 owns the invention.

derivation.reason: The two machine-checkable methods this project has are a platted corner and a traced waterline, and this seat is neither: it is a stated setback from a committed neighbouring building, on that building's own bearing, held clear of a committed corridor edge and tested against the committed heightfield. Every input is committed and the rule is written out in position.note, so it reproduces by hand; no derivation method in the schema can recompute it, and declaring one that could not would be worse than declaring none.

footprint.note: INVENTED. 2.4384 x 4.2672 m is 8 x 14 ft, inside family A5's band (6-8 ft front, 12-16 ft deep) - the crosswalk's small mixed utility outbuilding. Hides are hung to dry out of the sun and out of the rain, which wants a long narrow shed with air through it rather than a room. Nothing states that this yard had a drying shed. Every number is invented.

construction.note: Sawn boards nailed up vertically. Not `log` like the bark shed beside it, and the difference is the use: a drying shed is boarded so the gaps can be left, and a notched log pen cannot have gaps left in it. Invented.

wall_height_m.note: About 9 ft 2 in, above the archetype's size-aware default of 2.28 m for this plan, because hides hang full length from a rail and a 2.3 m wall drags them on the floor. What is reasoned is the range. Invented.

roof_type.note: 4.27 m of depth is inside the 5.0 m at which `default_roof_type` gives a shed roof. Invented.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The archetype's default for a shed roof; the rise over this run is 1.39 m against a 2.8 m wall. Invented.

board_gap_m.note: 50 mm between the siding boards, against the archetype's crude default of 12 mm. This is the one parameter that says what this building is for: a hide dries in moving air, so the boards are spaced on purpose, which is the same move `board_gap_m` exists for on a corn crib. It is well inside the archetype's own 0-150 mm bound. Invented - nothing describes the walls of any building in this yard.

door.note: One person with an armful, the archetype's `man` door. Invented.

door_side.note: The `front` elevation is the max-y wall, which at this bearing faces SOUTH, onto the yard between this shed and the tannery. Invented.

phases.change_note: One phase. This is a reconstruction of a works building the plant's own record says is missing, not a record of a building anybody named, so it has no history to divide into phases and inventing one would be inventing twice.

function.note: The closed vocabulary has no `drying shed`; `small_utility_building` is family A5's own term and the nearest it carries. The specific use is in the record's NAME and in this note. The use comes from the tannery's own record, which names 'drying sheds' among the things a tannery is and this model does not have. No occupant is claimed.

research_note: A RECONSTRUCTED YARD BUILDING AT THE SETTLEMENT'S FIRST FACTORY - T-1709, of T-1203. WHAT IS HELD: Andreas and DRLOIH for the tannery. WHAT IS INVENTED: this building and every attribute of it. WHAT IS STILL NOT MODELLED: the lime pits and tan vats. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE IT: any account of Miller and Hall's tanyard.
